690:     validate_intervals(ref_intervals, est_intervals)
691:     # When reference notes are empty, metrics are undefined, return 0's
692:     if len(ref_intervals) == 0 or len(est_intervals) == 0:
693:         return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
694: 
695:     matching = match_note_onsets(
696:         ref_intervals, est_intervals, onset_tolerance=onset_tolerance, strict=strict
697:     )
698: 
699:     onset_precision = float(len(matching)) / len(est_intervals)
700:     onset_recall = float(len(matching)) / len(ref_intervals)
701:     onset_f_measure = util.f_measure(onset_precision, onset_recall, beta=beta)
702:     return onset_precision, onset_recall, onset_f_measure
703: 
704: 
705: def offset_precision_recall_f1(
706:     ref_intervals,
707:     est_intervals,
708:     offset_ratio=0.2,
709:     offset_min_tolerance=0.05,
710:     strict=False,
711:     beta=1.0,
712: ):
713:     """Compute the Precision, Recall and F-measure of note offsets: an
714:     estimated offset is considered correct if it is within +-50ms (or 20% of
715:     the ref note duration, which ever is greater) of a reference offset. Note
716:     that this metric completely ignores note onsets and note pitch. This means
717:     an estimated offset will be considered correct if it matches a
718:     reference offset, even if the offsets come from notes with completely
719:     different pitches (i.e. notes that would not match with
720:     :func:`match_notes`).
721: 
722:     Examples
723:     --------
724:     >>> ref_intervals, _ = mir_eval.io.load_valued_intervals(
725:     ...     'reference.txt')
726:     >>> est_intervals, _ = mir_eval.io.load_valued_intervals(
727:     ...     'estimated.txt')
728:     >>> (offset_precision,
729:     ...  offset_recall,
730:     ...  offset_f_measure) = mir_eval.transcription.offset_precision_recall_f1(
731:     ...      ref_intervals, est_intervals)
732: 
733:     Parameters
734:     ----------
735:     ref_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n,2)
736:         Array of reference notes time intervals (onset and offset times)
737:     est_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(m,2)
738:         Array of estimated notes time intervals (onset and offset times)
739:     offset_ratio : float > 0 or None
740:         The ratio of the reference note's duration used to define the
741:         offset_tolerance. Default is 0.2 (20%), meaning the
742:         ``offset_tolerance`` will equal the ``ref_duration * 0.2``, or
743:         ``offset_min_tolerance`` (0.05 by default, i.e. 50 ms), whichever is
744:         greater.
745:     offset_min_tolerance : float > 0
746:         The minimum tolerance for offset matching. See ``offset_ratio``
747:         description for an explanation of how the offset tolerance is
748:         determined.
749:     strict : bool
750:         If ``strict=False`` (the default), threshold checks for onset matching
751:         are performed using ``<=`` (less than or equal). If ``strict=True``,
752:         the threshold checks are performed using ``<`` (less than).
753:     beta : float > 0
754:         Weighting factor for f-measure (default value = 1.0).
755: 
756:     Returns
757:     -------
758:     precision : float
759:         The computed precision score
760:     recall : float
761:         The computed recall score
762:     f_measure : float
763:         The computed F-measure score
764:     """
765:     validate_intervals(ref_intervals, est_intervals)
766:     # When reference notes are empty, metrics are undefined, return 0's
767:     if len(ref_intervals) == 0 or len(est_intervals) == 0:
768:         return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
769: 
770:     matching = match_note_offsets(
771:         ref_intervals,
772:         est_intervals,
773:         offset_ratio=offset_ratio,
774:         offset_min_tolerance=offset_min_tolerance,
775:         strict=strict,
776:     )
777: 
778:     offset_precision = float(len(matching)) / len(est_intervals)
779:     offset_recall = float(len(matching)) / len(ref_intervals)
780:     offset_f_measure = util.f_measure(offset_precision, offset_recall, beta=beta)
781:     return offset_precision, offset_recall, offset_f_measure
782: 
783: 
784: def evaluate(ref_intervals, ref_pitches, est_intervals, est_pitches, **kwargs):
785:     """Compute all metrics for the given reference and estimated annotations.
786: 
787:     Examples
788:     --------
789:     >>> ref_intervals, ref_pitches = mir_eval.io.load_valued_intervals(
790:     ...    'reference.txt')
791:     >>> est_intervals, est_pitches = mir_eval.io.load_valued_intervals(
792:     ...    'estimate.txt')
793:     >>> scores = mir_eval.transcription.evaluate(ref_intervals, ref_pitches,
794:     ...     est_intervals, est_pitches)
795: 
796:     Parameters
797:     ----------
798:     ref_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n,2)
799:         Array of reference notes time intervals (onset and offset times)
800:     ref_pitches : np.ndarray, shape=(n,)
801:         Array of reference pitch values in Hertz
802:     est_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(m,2)
803:         Array of estimated notes time intervals (onset and offset times)
804:     est_pitches : np.ndarray, shape=(m,)
805:         Array of estimated pitch values in Hertz
806:     **kwargs
807:         Additional keyword arguments which will be passed to the
808:         appropriate metric or preprocessing functions.
809: 
810:     Returns
811:     -------
812:     scores : dict
813:         Dictionary of scores, where the key is the metric name (str) and
814:         the value is the (float) score achieved.
815:     """
816:     # Compute all the metrics
817:     scores = collections.OrderedDict()
818: 
819:     # Precision, recall and f-measure taking note offsets into account
820:     kwargs.setdefault("offset_ratio", 0.2)
821:     orig_offset_ratio = kwargs["offset_ratio"]
822:     if kwargs["offset_ratio"] is not None:
823:         (
824:             scores["Precision"],
825:             scores["Recall"],
826:             scores["F-measure"],
827:             scores["Average_Overlap_Ratio"],
828:         ) = util.filter_kwargs(
829:             precision_recall_f1_overlap,
830:             ref_intervals,
831:             ref_pitches,
832:             est_intervals,
833:             est_pitches,
834:             **kwargs
835:         )
836: 
837:     # Precision, recall and f-measure NOT taking note offsets into account
838:     kwargs["offset_ratio"] = None
839:     (
840:         scores["Precision_no_offset"],
841:         scores["Recall_no_offset"],
842:         scores["F-measure_no_offset"],
843:         scores["Average_Overlap_Ratio_no_offset"],
844:     ) = util.filter_kwargs(
845:         precision_recall_f1_overlap,
